newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn closes lower on follow-through selling.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn closes lower on follow-through selling.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed lower on follow-through technical selling after Monday's slide with export news drawing mixed reviews, traders said.
Bearish input came from a purchase of corn by South Korea from China and Argentina and only a small purchase of corn from the U.S.
But corn futures were underpinned by a strong rally in nearby wheat futures plus USDA's weekly export inspections report, the traders said.
USDA Tuesday said U.S. corn inspected for export during the week ended January 16 totaled 42.012 million bushels.

That tally was above the previous week's level of 37.967 million bushels and above trade expectations for 30 million to 39 million bushels. But the U.S. corn export inspections pace for the 1996-97 marketing year at 740.343 million bushels remains well behind the previous year's pace of 937.860 million bushels.
"Funds bought corn again. Exports were good and that's helped, the market doesn't want to break," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter Reynolds.
Corn closed 1-1/2 cents per bushel lower to 1/4 higher, with March down 3/4 at $2.71.
